items.title: Will Verizon (VZ) Beat Estimates Again in Its Next Earnings Report?

items.title: 6 High-Yield Stocks Where the Market May Be Warning of a Dividend Cut
items.summary: A fat dividend yield can mean a generous payout or a stock the market has already written off, and right now six familiar names are flashing signals that suggest the difference matters more than ever.

items.title: Treasury Yields Are Above 5%. These 4 Dividend Stocks Still Make the Cut
items.summary: A 5% Treasury yield raises the bar for every dividend stock in a retirement portfolio, but four large-cap payers in real estate, telecom, tobacco, and healthcare are generating the cash flow to prove they still belong.

items.title: A $500,000 Roth Portfolio Loaded With These Dividend Stocks Pays $40,000 a Year and the IRS Gets None of It
items.summary: The IRS collects thousands of dollars a year from dividend investors who never stopped to ask which account their income stocks actually live in. Six high-yield names reveal exactly how much that placement question costs at every tax bracket.

items.title: Can Corning's AT&T Deal Boost Its Optical Communications Growth?

items.title: AT&T Declines 13.9% in Six Months: How to Play the Stock?
items.summary: T faces stiff competition, legacy revenue declines and heavy debt, but fiber expansion, wireless growth and bundled services offer potential offsets.

items.title: Verizon Communications (VZ) Adds Charles Phillips To Its Board
items.summary: Verizon Communications (NYSE:VZ) has elected technology executive and private equity investor Charles Phillips to its Board of Directors. The Federal Communications Commission has placed a hold on Verizon's plan for automatic shutdown of copper-based telephone service in parts of New Jersey. The Board addition of Phillips and the FCC pause on copper service retirement frame broader questions about Verizon's technology focus and legacy network strategy. items.title: 3 Consumer Stocks We Approach with Caution
items.summary: The performance of consumer discretionary businesses is closely linked to economic cycles. Over the past six months, it seems like demand may be facing some headwinds as the industry’s 3.9% return has lagged the S&P 500 by 17.2 percentage points.
